subject: Economic tradeoff: flat discount vs ramp credits for vendor replacement
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Amara Lewis <amara@merchretail.com>, procurement <procurement@merchretail.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Economic tradeoff: flat discount vs ramp credits for vendor replacement

Hi Amara / procurement team,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per your ask, attached is a concise model that lays out two concrete structures for switching from your incumbent inference vendor to Redwood:

Option A — Ramp credits (migration-first):
- 30% credit on consumed inference spend for the first 90 days (applies to tokenized usage).
- Additional $50k professional services credit to cover integration and benchmark testing.
- No long-term discount afterwards; pricing reverts to standard committed list.

Option B — Time-bound flat discount (smooth pricing):
- 10% off list price for 12 months across all inference and embedding units.
- Includes 1 day/week priority support during first 3 months.
- No separate onboarding credit.

Tradeoffs for your team: ramp credits favor heavy initial consumption and reduce go-live cash impact; flat discount lowers costs predictably but requires a stronger commitment horizon to hit savings parity. I attached the pricing-model workbook with example run rates using the usage numbers you shared.

Next steps: can you confirm which structure you prefer (A or B) and whether you want an explicit pilot (canary) for the first 30 days? If you like, we can also propose a hybrid.

Attachments: 2026-11-29_pricing-model.xlsx (xls/x)

From: Amara Lewis <amara@merchretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Economic tradeoff: flat discount vs ramp credits for vendor replacement

Marcus —

Thanks for the clear options and the workbook. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:
1) How does the ramp credit interact with our monthly committed minimums? If we take option A, does the 30% reduce our committed target or is it applied as a post-facto credit?
2) For option B, can that 10% be applied only to inference (not embeddings)? We run embeddings across other workloads and want to keep pricing isolated.
3) Security question: is Redwood willing to include a 72-hour SLA for any pilot failures during the go-live window? Our legal/procurement will need to see that.

If you can answer those, we can move to an internal approval loop. Ideally we want the commercial terms in writing by EoD Thursday.

—Amara
Head of Platform Procurement
Mercury Retail

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Economic tradeoff: flat discount vs ramp credits for vendor replacement

Jordan / Lauren — quick internal. Amara's procurement questions above. We need an approved guardrail to present by Thursday. My proposal (high level):

- Ramp credit mechanics: apply as a post-facto consumption credit (invoiced amount reduced), not as a reduction to committed minimums. That keeps quarter revenue true but gives customer immediate relief.
- Option B isolation: allow 10% to be scoped to inference only (embeddings excluded).
- Pilot SLA: provide a 72-hour incident response target for pilot window; we will not extend formal SLA credits until go-live under committed plan.

Tradeoffs and ask:
- If we do ramp credits, offer 30% up to a $250k cap OR
- Offer a hybrid: 20% ramp credit for first 60 days + 7.5% flat discount for first 12 months, contingent on a 6-month minimal commit (this reduces risk on both sides).

Please review the attached pricing-model.xlsx — I need a short, client-facing summary we can send that calls out the hybrid as the recommended path. If you think we should push harder on the cap or the duration, say so.

Thanks — Marcus
Sales Director, Redwood Inference
Attachment: 2026-11-29_pricing-model.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Economic tradeoff: flat discount vs ramp credits for vendor replacement

Agree with Marcus but recommend the hybrid as the client-facing default. Quick justification and numbers:

Recommended commercial (client-facing):
- Hybrid Offer: 20% ramp credit on consumed inference for first 60 days (applied as post-facto credit), capped at $150,000.
- Plus 7.5% flat discount on inference list price for 12 months (embeddings excluded).
- Customer must sign a 6-month minimum consumption commitment OR accept a reduced PS package if they keep it month-to-month.
- We include a $30k professional services voucher to accelerate model compatibility tests and the canary run.

Why this works:
- Preserves revenue recognition (credit applied after invoicing).
- Lowers switching friction with a meaningful immediate credit but keeps upside beyond the cap.
- Predictable ongoing discount reduces procurement churn and simplifies QBR conversations.

Operational guardrails to include in the proposal:
- Pilot SLA: 72-hour on-call response; formal SLA triggers only after go-live on committed plan.
- Fallback: if runtime regressions exceed defined thresholds during pilot (latency 2x baseline or >3% error rate), we will provide extended PS support and a one-time remediation credit.

I created a short summary PDF (ramp-credit-summary.pdf) that pulls the math into a one-pager — attach that for the procurement thread.

—Jordan
VP Sales Engineering

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Amara Lewis <amara@merchretail.com>, procurement <procurement@merchretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Final proposal: hybrid migration package for Mercury Retail (DEAL-7831)

Amara — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on your procurement questions and our internal review, here is the proposal we recommend and are ready to commit to in writing: 

Final commercial (DEAL-7831):
- Hybrid Offer (recommended): 20% ramp credit on consumed inference for the first 60 days, applied as a credit on invoices, capped at $150,000.
- 7.5% flat discount on inference list price for 12 months (embeddings explicitly excluded).
- $30,000 professional services voucher to be used for integration, benchmark validation, and canary tuning.
- Pilot SLA: 72-hour initial response target during pilot; formal SLA credit triggers begin upon activation of the committed plan.
- Commit: 6-month minimum consumption commitment for the discount to apply (we can structure this as a soft commit tied to forecast and quarterly review).

Attachments: ramp-credit-summary.pdf, pricing-model workbook. HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/78910. DocuSign for the commercial addendum: https://www.docusign.com/link/abc123

If you sign the addendum by Friday EoD PST we can prioritize onboarding in the January engineering window and fast-track the $30k PS voucher. Please let me know if you want any of the numbers tightened (cap, percent, or duration) — happy to discuss.

Best,
